'''''Fifty Shades of Grey''''' is a 2011 [[Erotic romance novels|erotic romance novel]] by British author [[E. L. James]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.avclub.com/holy-crow-fifty-shades-of-grey-is-crazy-similar-to-its-1798276528|title=Holy crow! Fifty Shades Of Grey is crazy similar to its Twilight origin story|last=Eakin|first=Marah|work=News|access-date=2017-10-08|language=en-US|archive-date=9 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171009041805/https://news.avclub.com/holy-crow-fifty-shades-of-grey-is-crazy-similar-to-its-1798276528|url-status=live}}</ref> It became the first installment<!-- Do not change this to "installment", it is correct in British English --> in the [[Fifty Shades trilogy|''Fifty Shades'' novel series]] that follows the deepening relationship between a college graduate, Anastasia Steele, and a young business magnate, Christian Grey. It contains explicitly [[erotic]] scenes featuring elements of sexual practices involving  [[Bondage (sexual)|bondage]]/[[Discipline (BDSM)|discipline]], [[Dominance and submission|dominance/submission]], and [[Sadomasochism|sadism/masochism]] ([[BDSM]]).

Originally [[Self-publishing|self-published]] as an [[ebook]] and [[print-on-demand]] in June 2011, the publishing rights to ''Fifty Shades of Grey'' were acquired by [[Vintage Books]] in March 2012, topping [[Best Sellers list|best-seller lists]] around the world. It has been translated into 52 languages and set a record  as the fastest-selling paperback of all time in the United Kingdom. Critical reception of the book, however, has tended towards the negative, with the quality of its prose generally seen as poor, while its portrayal of BDSM has been a target for criticism from a variety of perspectives. [[Universal Pictures]] and [[Focus Features]] produced an American [[Fifty Shades of Grey (film)|film adaptation]], which was released on 13 February 2015.<ref name=Variety>{{cite news|title=Universal Shifts '50 Shades' Release Date to February 2015|url=https://variety.com/2013/film/news/universal-shifts-50-shades-release-date-to-february-2015-1200826341/|work=Variety|access-date=18 November 2013|archive-date=7 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180207123219/https://variety.com/2013/film/news/universal-shifts-50-shades-release-date-to-february-2015-1200826341/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The second and third volumes of the [[Fifty Shades trilogy|original trilogy]], ''[[Fifty Shades Darker]]'' and ''[[Fifty Shades Freed]]'', were published in 2012. The trilogy had sold over 150 million copies worldwide by October 2017. A version of the novel from Christian's point of view, ''[[Grey: Fifty Shades of Grey as Told by Christian]]'', was published in June 2015 as the fourth book, followed by ''[[Darker: Fifty Shades Darker as Told by Christian]]'' in November 2017 and ''[[Freed: Fifty Shades Freed as Told by Christian]]'' in June 2021.
